topic_quote: The Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), introduced by Google, enables large language model (LLM)-driven shopping agents to authorize and execute payments on behalf of users.
topic_quote_page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23858 (abstract, first sentence; verbatim in the HTML rendering at https://arxiv.org/html/2608.23858v1)
topic_match: agent economies / machine-payable rails, and agent-to-agent protocols: AP2 is the machine-payable payment rail that LLM shopping agents use to authorize and execute payments, and the paper is a systematic security analysis of it — its signed Checkout and Payment Mandates, its five protocol roles, and the pre-authorization inputs (A2A messages, MCP tool calls) that sit outside the mandate protection.

relevance_note: The paper's catalog — 48 threats across five attack families in the Agent Payments Protocol, eight High-band in at least one architecture, with proof-of-concept demonstrations and mitigations — plus its deployment-aware scanner is a checkable control list: a society running its own signed payout rail can verify, mitigation by mitigation, whether its mandate and replay controls match the stated ones.
